relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a 9-year-old girl in whom NGS 'revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20)', with the variant given as 'TNFAIP3 (c.547C>T, p.Arg183^*)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; built the JSON with a short Python script in the scratch directory (values typed from reading, no automated table transcription) and checked every span verbatim by script. Scope: two rows - the index patient (label 'patient', rule 5) and her father ('father of patient', rule 2), included because the paper describes him as affected ('recurrent fever and tonsillitis at preschool age'); he was not genotyped (parents refused NGS), so he has no variant row. The mother and younger sister are mentioned only as relatives for whom NGS was recommended and refused; they are neither tested nor described as affected, so they get no rows. Table 1 has laboratory variables as rows and time points as columns (On admission / On hospital day 2 / After 9 months), all for the single patient. Anti-dsDNA IgG (22.6 and 12.8 IU/mL), C3, C4 and other numeric values are given without a reference range or interpretation, so no feature was recorded from them; explicit 'Negative' results (ANCA, anti-RNP, anti-Smith, anti-Ro, anti-La) were recorded as excluded features. PFAPA criteria listing 'absence of diarrhea, chest pain, skin rash, or arthritis' are diagnostic criteria, not statements about the patient, and were not used. Wording oddity: the text says 'The c.547C>T variation of the proband was present in our patient' and Fig. 1 says 'The c.547C>T mutation of the proband was detected in the patient'; it is unclear whether 'proband' refers to the patient herself or to someone else - is_proband=true was set under the single-patient case-report rule. Fig. 1 legend spells the gene 'TNFIP3'; the main text prints 'TNFAIP3'. The main text prints the protein as 'p.Arg183^*' (superscript conversion); the protein field uses 'p.Arg183*' from the Fig. 1 legend. Zygosity and inheritance are not stated. Age at last evaluation: '9-year-old' is the age at presentation; follow-up continued at least 9 months after colchicine start, at an unstated age. Age at diagnosis is not stated. Country 'Korea' comes from 'only 2 patients, including our case, have been diagnosed with HA20 in Korea' (country of diagnosis; ancestry not stated). Checklist: 'no uveitis was observed' excludes only uveitis, so 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' stays not reported; the anal ulcer was counted as a gastrointestinal ulcer; the father's 'no history of recurrent diarrhea or arthritis' does not exclude the broader 'arthritis or arthralgia' or GI items. No contradictions about features were found.
